sentences.text: The respondents initiated the proceedings against the present petitioner by taking a sample on 07.04.2001.
The sample was manufactured on 03.02.2001 with an expiry of six months.
The analysis was done by the concerned authority and a report was filed regarding the adulteration.
The information of the report was given to the present petitioner on 06.05.2004 when the complaint was lodged.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has stated that Section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 provides for re-analysis within 10 days of the adulterated report being brought to the knowledge of the adulterator at his instance.
Admittedly, the provision for re-analysis is defeated on account of the fact that the product had expired within six months from 03.02.2001.
Since, the re-analysis could not have been done on 06.04.2004, therefore, the mandatory provision of Section 13 (2) stands defeated.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment of S.S. Sujalal Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, reported in 2002(2) FAC 83, in which the Hon'ble Andhra Pradesh High Court has laid down the following case law :-
"Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. praying that in the circumstances stated in the Criminal Petition the High Court wil be pleased to quash the proceedings in STC No.04/2002 on the file of the (3 of 5) Court of the Additional Munsif Magistrate,
Adoni, Kurnool District.

sentences.text: The Petition coming on for hearing upon perusing the petition and upon hearing the arguments of Mr.P. Vengala Reddy, Advocate for the petitioner and of the Public Prosecutor on behalf of the respondent.

THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING ORDER :-
This is a petition to quash the proceedings in STC No.4 of 2002 on the file of the Court of the Additional Munsif Magistrate, Adoni, filed under Section 16(1)(a)(i), 7(i)
and 2(ia)(m) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

From the charge sheet it is seen that sample of the mineral water was taken on 18.09.1999 and was sent for analysis and the Analysis Report Dt.20.09.1999 was received by the Food Inspector on 30.09.1999 and the complaint was filed on 03.12.2001 and was taken cognizance of 02.02.2002 and the copy of the Analysis Report was sent to petitioner on 20.02.2002.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that since the shelf life of the water,
sample of which was taken by the Food Inspector, was only six months and since the copy of the report of the Analysis was not served on the petitioner till 20.02.2002 though it was received by the Food Inspector on 30.09.1999,, the petitioner lost a valuable right to send the sample for analysis by the Central Food Laboratory and hence the prosecution is liable to be quashed.

2

Since the shelf life of the water is only six months and since the analysis report was not sent to the petitioner till February, 2002 though the report was received towards the end of September, 1999 the petitioner lost a valuable right to sent the sample for (4 of 5) analysis to the Central Food Laboratory for re- analysis, thereby prejudice has been caused to the petitioner.

Therefore, the prosecution is liable to be quashed, and hence the petition is allowed and the proceedings in STC No.4 of 2002 of the file of the court of the Additional Munsif Magistrate, Adoni against the petitioner are quashed.

"
5. Learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the submission and stated that since, the second sample was not delayed, therefore, the provision of delay for re-analysis will not apply in the present case.
6.

After hearing counsel for the petitioner and perusing the record of the case, this court is of the opinion that Section 13(2) categorically provides an opportunity to the accused persons of re-analysis on being given the report of adulteration on the first analysis.

Since, the first analysis itself was done in time and its report was also receiving well within time on 08.05.2001, therefore, the respondents were under a legal obligation arising out of Section 13 (2) of the Act of 1954 to have provided such information to the petitioner so as to enable him to go for re- analysis in accordance with Section 13 of the Act of 1954.

Since, the mandatory provision of re-analysis could not be materialized as the production which is water was manufactured on 03.02.2001 and would have expired within a period of six months, therefore, any re-analysis on or after 06.04.2004 would not confirm to the requirement of the re-analysis, which is a clear provision for the accused persons to take a defence on account of the adulteration.

In light of the aforesaid observations, the present misc. petition is allowed and consequently, the complaint pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pali,, in criminal case No.33/2004 in the matter of State VS. Ram Kumar Agarwal & Ors.
